candidates.title: Norval Morrisseau masterwork not seen for 40 years unveiled at Thunder Bay Art Gallery
candidates.description: After 40 years in storage, a rare masterwork painting by Ojibway artist Norval Morrisseau has been unveiled at the Thunder Bay Art Gallery in northwestern Ontario. The painting is on loan from EA Studios Calgary, and is described as "very spiritual" and "very powerful."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Never giving up': Alberta separatist leaders say referendum vote won't end their fight
candidates.description: Premier Danielle Smith and her government expect next month's separation referendum to be the last word on the subject — but those fighting for an independent Alberta say no matter the outcome, the fight goes on.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Supreme Court says it invalidated Liberal MP's 1-vote win due to Elections Canada error
candidates.description: The Supreme Court of Canada says it decided to invalidate a federal Liberal candidate's one-vote victory in the 2025 federal election to ensure public trust in the electoral process.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pickleball courts cause uproar in this normally quiet community in Port Stanley, Ont.
candidates.description: Tensions are rising between residents of the Kokomo Park community in Port Stanley, Ont., and it's all because of pickleball. While the public courts are popular with players, some neighbours consider them a nuisance. A petition and even threats of legal action are involved.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Windsor, Ont., police now charging people using illegal drugs in public despite prosecution uncertainty
candidates.description: For years, federal lawyers have been instructed to avoid prosecuting people who openly use illegal drugs in public. Now, Windsor, Ont., police are stopping to arrest them. Here's why the service decided to lay charges and track how many cases make it through the courts.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: At first, Rick Hansen fought the idea of a wheelchair. But then it became a vehicle for his freedom
candidates.description: At first, Rick Hansen saw his wheelchair as a symbol of limitations, eschewing what would eventually help propel him around the globe and shatter the true barriers: stigma and a world designed for the able-bodied. When he overcame that, it became a vehicle for his freedom and advocacy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Parents of NHL prospect hospitalized after collapse at team workout say he's a 'fighter'
candidates.description: The parents of Ontario prospect Matthew Mayich, who was drafted by the St. Louis Blues, are hoping for a miracle. The young hockey player is in hospital in critical condition.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Starbucks workers in Hamilton hope to tackle wage, customer harassment issues in negotiating 1st contract
candidates.description: A group of Hamilton Starbucks workers who joined United Steelworkers this month aims to address issues including harassment by customers and an unclear wage structure as they prepare to negotiate their first collective agreement, the union and a worker told CBC Hamilton.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montreal mayor mulls legal action against Quebec after baby found at encampment
candidates.description: News of a baby being found living with its mother in an encampment on Notre-Dame Street last week sparked strong reaction from Montreal's mayor and Quebec's party leaders on Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Marineland beluga from Niagara Falls, Ont., dies at Spain aquarium, 3rd death after rescue transfer
candidates.description: A beluga in Spain that was part of the massive relocation of animals from the shuttered Marineland park in Niagara Falls, Ont., has died. Two other belugas died within weeks of being moved to the U.S.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Cocaine eyes' to cash bribes: 5 revelations from Project South wiretaps
candidates.description: A police officer doing drugs before his shift, a trunk full of police uniforms to sell, details on drug deals and plans to open massage parlours are some of the revelations Project South investigators captured through wiretaps as part of their sweeping corruption probe, according to newly reportable details from an Information to Obtain (ITO) application in the case.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: As Carney's popularity soars, Conservatives weigh what to do about their own leader
candidates.description: A number of Conservative MPs have soured on Pierre Poilievre as leader, but despite this growing angst, his position is relatively secure because there is no strong appetite to oust him and choose someone new right now, according to party and caucus sources who spoke to CBC News.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ‘I feel so betrayed’: Iranian conscripts in Canada face deportation threats over terrorist designation
candidates.description: Hundreds of Iranian families have received a letter from the federal immigration department, declaring them inadmissible to Canada. As frustrations grow, time is running out for them to prove they are not members of a terrorist organization.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa mayoral candidate charged for alleged death threats against Doug Ford and Mark Sutcliffe
candidates.description: A candidate for mayor of Ottawa is facing multiple charges for allegedly making death threats against Ontario Premier Doug Ford and incumbent Ottawa Mayor Mark Sutcliffe earlier this month.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: She pressed charges against a Mountie for sex assault, but says court delays robbed her of justice
candidates.description: A sexual assault case against RCMP Const. William McNutt was dropped because of delays in the justice system. The complainant says if restorative justice had been an option, she would have taken it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Deepfake doctors peddling bogus cures are becoming more convincing — and very little can be done to stop them
candidates.description: Physicians warn AI-generated ads featuring the likenesses of prominent doctors are scamming patients out of their money, putting Canadians’ health at risk and eroding public trust. Yet there’s still no clear method to get deepfake videos taken down. scamming patients out of their money, putting Canadians' health at risk, and eroding public trust
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: More than 500,000 Albertans have applied to vote by mail in referendum: Elections Alberta
candidates.description: More than half a million Albertans have requested to vote by mail in the upcoming referendum, according to Elections Alberta.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Manitoba adopts permanent daylight time after survey suggested overwhelming opposition to clock changes
candidates.description: Manitobans no longer need to remember to spring forward or fall back one hour on their clocks, as Premier Wab Kinew says the province will adopt permanent daylight time.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The invasive spotted lanternfly has been officially detected in Canada for the first time
candidates.description: An invasive insect known to kill grapevines and impact other crops and trees has been detected for the first time in Canada by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA). And that first detection happened in Windsor.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ex-B.C. Conservative MLAs and party president say a private investigator was hired to look into them
candidates.description: The former B.C. Conservative party president says she was one of about a dozen people, including four MLAs, who were targeted by a private investigator allegedly hired by the party’s former executive director.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's top general is up for a senior NATO post. Will Trump get in her way?
candidates.description: Canada's Gen. Jennie Carignan faces Germany's Gen. Carsten Breuer on Saturday in a secret-ballot contest to chair NATO's Military Committee. A victory would make Carignan the first woman to hold the post and return Canada to the chair after nearly two decades, amid Ottawa's push for deeper ties with Europe.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Germany's far-right AfD party is taking pages out of Trump's playbook
candidates.description: From creating a deportation task force to revising history lessons in schools, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which won a resounding victory in the state of Saxony-Anhlat last week and could soon hold power, wants to implement policies that echo some of those enacted by U.S. President Donald Trump.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ICE agent pleads not guilty to lying to FBI about shooting of man in Minneapolis
candidates.description: The top prosecutor from Minnesota's Hennepin County announced the arrest Friday of an ICE officer charged for shooting a Venezuelan-born man in January at the height of a deadly immigration blitz launched by the Trump administration.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Indonesian divers recover 3 bodies from capsized ferry as salvage operation begins
candidates.description: Rescue teams in Indonesia on Friday recovered three bodies from a capsized ferry while preparing to salvage the wreckage of the accident, bringing the confirmed death toll to nine, with 126 people still missing, officials said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: At least 21 killed in Pakistan mosque bombing near police station
candidates.description: A vehicle bomb exploded Friday at a mosque near police offices in northwestern Pakistan as gunmen tried to storm the compound, killing at least 21 people and wounding 80 others, police and rescue officials said. Among those killed and wounded were police officers attending prayers at the mosque.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Philippines school shooting leaves 2 students, gunman dead
candidates.description: Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New cat species identified for the 1st time in a century
candidates.description: A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia's cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living cat species has been formally named and described in more than a century.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russians begin voting in parliamentary election set to cement Kremlin's power
candidates.description: Russians on Friday began three days of voting in the country's first wartime parliamentary election, which features virtually no opposition and is all but certain to secure the Kremlin's political dominance.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UN mission finds 'grounds to believe' U.S. committed war crimes in strikes on Iranian school, sports centre
candidates.description: A United Nations fact-finding mission on Iran said on Thursday it had reasonable grounds to believe the United States was behind two military strikes on a school ‌and sports facility in Iran in February and that these constituted war crimes.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Blood is on our hands': Haitian honour student's death sparks outcry over ICE ankle monitors
candidates.description: Pierre Damas Bel fled Haiti and came to the U.S. with a dream of becoming a neurosurgeon. But after U.S. immigration authorities fitted the 20-year-old university student with an ankle monitor, he felt he was "treated like an animal" — and died weeks later when he walked into highway traffic.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Far-right German politician heckles Carney with 'U.S.A.' chant before EU address
candidates.description: As Prime Minister Mark Carney approached the podium at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, he was met by a lone heckler with an unexpected chant for a Canadian leader speaking to the EU in France.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge orders Kennedy Center to give 30-day notice before any major changes — including demolition
candidates.description: A U.S. federal judge on Thursday ordered the Kennedy Center to provide 30-day notice before making any major physical changes to the building, including demolishing it as President Donald Trump has threatened to do.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: OpenAI asks California court to dismiss lawsuits over Tumbler Ridge shooting
candidates.description: Lawyers for OpenAI claim any legal action related to the deaths and injuries should take place in British Columbia.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Australian athlete apologizes for racing with diarrhea, forfeits the Beijing competition she won
candidates.description: Australian Joanna Wietrzyk, who started a global uproar after soiling herself and leaking feces at the popular indoor fitness competition, has apologized for continuing to race and forfeited her win.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alex Ovechkin says he's 'for peace and love' after appearing in ad for Putin-aligned party
candidates.description: Alex Ovechkin says he's "for peace and love" after the Russian hockey star appeared in an ad for a party aligned with President Vladimir Putin during the off-season.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: EU's offer to Canada is proof that Europe is ready to stand up to Trump, says lawmaker
candidates.description: The European Union's overtures to Canada are a signal that Europe is ready to take off the boxing gloves when it comes to dealing with U.S. President Donald Trump, says a German member of the European Parliament.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: King Charles warns AI leaders of 'existential dangers'
candidates.description: King Charles hosted executives from AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic, as well as chipmaker Nvidia and the Google DeepMind AI research laboratory, in Scotland, and urged them to apply safeguards to their products 'before it is all too late.'
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russian missile and drone strikes on Ukraine injure at least 16, including children
candidates.description: A Russian barrage of missiles and drones targeting Ukraine's capital and the surrounding region injured at least 16 people overnight and into Thursday morning, local authorities said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: These documentarians got a standing ovation in Venice, but their fellow Israelis are furious
candidates.description: The documentary film NAZA is stirring outrage in Israel, prompting many to defend their military's actions in Gaza against accusations it approves strikes regardless of harm to Palestinian civilians, while the filmmakers question why critical reflection is being stonewalled.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Rogue AI swarm used a University of Toronto link-shortening tool to communicate
candidates.description: A swarm of rogue OpenAI agents that hijacked a German website in the spring reportedly also used at least 10 other websites for unsanctioned communications earlier this year, including a link-shortening tool at the University of Toronto.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Gas prices are dropping. You can thank the 'winter blend' for that
candidates.description: After ticking up earlier this week, gas prices dropped by about eight cents overnight, and could fall by a few more by the weekend according to one expert. But diesel is soaring, which could be bad news — even for those who don't drive.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada and the EU are getting cosy. These charts show how our economies stack up
candidates.description: Canada is likely to strengthen trade ties with Europe. Here are some charts that show how Canada’s economy is faring compared to its (perhaps future associate) peers in Europe.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Don't close, don't sell': Union implores Stellantis to keep Brampton plant as automaker signals sale
candidates.description: The union representing Canadian workers at Stellantis is urging the automaker to keep its commitment to retooling its Brampton Ont., plant as the company looks poised to sell it instead.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ford, Joly call on Stellantis to make new model at Brampton plant after automaker signals potential sale
candidates.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford and federal Industry Minister Mélanie Joly are calling on Stellantis to produce a new model at its idled Brampton, Ont., assembly plant after the automaker signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel on its potential sale.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Three dead and eight injured in Philippines school shooting
candidates.description: The gunman is among the dead in what is the third school shooting in the country since June.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Shots heard as police start moving migrants from Ceuta beaches
candidates.description: Police reportedly fired into the air on Friday morning as they struggled to contain crowds jostling to secure a place at the tented site.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror says he had no doubt she deliberately killed her children
candidates.description: It is the first time the juror, who refused to side with the others and acquit Clancy, has spoken publicly about his decision.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
candidates.description: A four-year-old child is among those killed in the attack, during which gunmen also opened fire on a police facility.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ronaldo named in first Portugal squad since World Cup - at age of 41
candidates.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus for their upcoming Nations League games.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Dozens of suspected illegal miners die in Nigerian custody
candidates.description: Authorities linked the deaths to disease, but this has been disputed by intelligence reports and relatives of the accused.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy
candidates.description: Many Nigerians buy their first ever shares - in the oil refinery owned by Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Zara Larsson criticises White House for using her song in deportation video
candidates.description: The White House removed Larsson's Midnight Sun from one of its reels after the artist called the clip "dehumanising".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Canadians dream of Europe as Carney floats longshot plan for living and working in EU
candidates.description: Torontonians are excited by the possibility of moving to the EU, even if it is unlikely anytime soon.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: This Olympic river has 500 crocodiles in it - but that's not the main concern
candidates.description: Queensland's Fitzroy River has been selected for the 2032 Games, despite concerns over the course - and its inhabitants.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Verified video shows wreckage of Saudi fighter jet shot down over Yemen
candidates.description: BBC Verify tracks down the location of a Houthi video showing the wreckage of an F-15 they claim to have shot down.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Rosenberg: Russia's elections will have few surprises, but for the Kremlin they matter
candidates.description: There is no doubt over the outcome of this vote, but for the Kremlin they are still an important moment.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Is Canada about to join the EU?
candidates.description: Ties between Canada and the European Union have been getting closer as trade dispute with the US continue.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Inside Singapore's 'Fort Knox' for city's $2bn dirty money auction
candidates.description: The BBC goes inside a fortified storage facility to view luxury goods seized by police that are now up for auction.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Leaked photos reveal extensive damage at US bases in Gulf
candidates.description: The photos, provided by active military personnel, show a severed radar jet, flattened trailers and severely damaged buildings as a result of Iranian strikes.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands
candidates.description: The comments were made at a summit in Ayrshire with participants from AI giants including Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Uncontrolled AI could lead to 'silicon species' rivalling humans, warns Microsoft
candidates.description: Mustafa Suleyman says he believes rival AI firm Anthropic is in effect teaching Claude it "may be conscious".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC
candidates.description: Evan Spiegel says it would be "an important step forward for the industry" in an interview with the BBC.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: See tiny organisms on show in microscopic video competition
candidates.description: The winning video features tiny hair-like structures, called cilia, in the airways of a child with a rare genetic disease.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund
candidates.description: A new study says climate change was a likely factor in the massive flood on the Nepal-Tibet border last month.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The farmer who turned to singing after bovine TB silenced his fields
candidates.description: Dairy farmer Mervyn Kelso struggled with the sadness of the empty fields when he lost his entire herd to bovine TB.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Move faster to solve climate challenges, Prince William says
candidates.description: The Prince of Wales tells the BBC we need to "accelerate" in finding solutions to climate challenges as Earthshot nominees are unveiled.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Will even one of the U.N.'s 17 'sustainable development goals' be met by 2030?
candidates.description: The 17 goals agreed upon by world leaders are incredibly ambitious. Are we even close to achieving any of them? If we don't, is the project a failure?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Judge says Trump can't demolish Kennedy Center. And, lawsuits target voter intimidation
candidates.description: A federal judge ruled yesterday that President Trump cannot tear down the Kennedy Center without a 30-day notice. And, recent lawsuits seek to keep armed federal officers away from polling sites.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
candidates.description: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: South Africa 'feels like a prison' for women amid spate of femicides
candidates.description: South Africa has some of the highest rates of violence against women in the world, and a spate of killings of nine women in the same area in recent weeks has led to renewed outrage.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Poland's prime minister warns of Russian 'accidental' attacks on Ukraine's allies
candidates.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that these potential strikes "intend to paralyze NATO" in an attempt to demonstrate that Article 5 "exists only in theory."
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What to know after a week of Houthi attacks that threaten Saudi oil
candidates.description: The Houthis' biggest land grab in years reignited Yemen's 12-year civil war and pushed up global fuel prices, extending their reach to a key maritime chokepoint and threatening Saudi Arabia's oil exports.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Behind the overture from the European Union to Canada
candidates.description: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with Ian Bremmer, president and founder of the Eurasia Group, about the latest developments between Canada, the European Union and the U.S.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: To prevent deaths in childbirth, Kenyan moms turn to an AI powered chatbot
candidates.description: Many questions come up during pregnancy. Is swelling normal? Are avocados safe to eat? For folks in Kenya who don't have a search engine at their fingertips, a chatbot is offering a lifeline.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Greetings from Beijing, where baozi are worth the wait in line
candidates.description: The popular fluffy steamed buns are filled with pork, vegetables, tofu — and in one trendy Beijing shop, chocolate and red beans.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.N.-backed experts cite possible U.S. war crimes in Iran, including a school attack
candidates.description: Human rights experts commissioned by the U.N. say they have found "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes in Iran, including a strike on a school in the southern city of Minab.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
candidates.description: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
candidates.description: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A bad year for the crypto industry just got a lot worse
candidates.description: The cryptocurrency industry just suffered a major defeat in a bill they had badly wanted to get through the Senate. It's the latest setback in a terrible year for the sector.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Doctors raise concerns about views and experience of members on federal task force
candidates.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. names new members to powerful federal task force that plays a key role in determining the kind of preventive case people get. In a major departure, the new members of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force include specialists instead of experts on preventive care and general medicine, raising fears among many doctors.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A year ago, President Trump pledged to lower Medicaid drug prices. Has that happened?
candidates.description: The Trump administration's efforts to lower drug prices included promised changes to Medicaid. But it's still unclear which drugs will be affected. And each state has to opt in.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump's surgeon general pick faces questions on vaccines and vaping at Senate hearing
candidates.description: The Senate committee on health held a confirmation hearing for three top health officials, including surgeon general. Dr. Nicole Saphier is President Trump's third pick to be the nation's top doctor.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why reshaping memories may hold the key to raising self-esteem
candidates.description: In a new book, psychologist Marisa Franco explains why it's good to feel good about yourself — and shares a helpful memory technique that we've turned into a printable worksheet.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Here's why an Arizona medical examiner is working to track heat-related deaths
candidates.description: No one across the U.S. is consistently tracking climate-fueled deaths. One medical examiner has a new protocol on heat-deaths.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ectopic Pregnancy Deaths
candidates.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with ProPublica data reporter Andrea Suozzo about their investigation looking into the rise in deaths related to ectopic pregnancies.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: M 6.5 - 169 km W of Nikolski, Alaska
candidates.description: The United States Geological Survey reported an earthquake of magnitude 6.5. The event occurred near 169 km W of Nikolski, Alaska. Official monitoring data may be updated as scientists review additional measurements.
candidates.author: U.S. Geological Survey

candidates.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation
candidates.description: Coding agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot manipulation: a language model writes the robot controller as a program, and agents built in this way now operate robots without robot-specific training.Whether this paradigm is also safe, however, has not been asked. We evaluate coding agent under a safety constraint, where each task pairs a manipulation goal with an obstacle the robot must not touch. The agent pursues the goal but collides with the obstacle in most cases, treating task completion as its sole objective while neglecting safety. The agent reasons about the obstacle in its traces, and the prompt already forbids touching it, so neither perception nor instruction is at fault; the fault lies in the planning, where the stated constraint never becomes a priority. By decomposing manipulation into a route phase and a contact-rich moment, we locate the source of the failure. Along the route, the model cannot prioritize the safety constraint, having no notion of a clearing route and none of replanning once a chosen route becomes infeasible. At the contact, it is unaware that contact execution is bounded by the same constraint. To close this gap, we present SafeHarness, which equips the model with two obstacle-aware harnesses that enable it to prioritize the safety constraint. Obstacle-aware route planning grounds the objects as bounding boxes and draws candidate routes over them as sequences of waypoints. The agent then plans a route in advance, verifies it, replans when necessary, and only then executes it. Obstacle-aware contact execution instead selects the contact position so that the contact itself avoids the obstacle. SafeHarness attains 71.9% task success and 87.5% collision avoidance, surpassing the previous SOTA by 6.5% and 27.0%, respectively. These results are $2.3\times$ and $1.5\times$ those of the same agent without harnesses.
candidates.author: Bingxin Xu, Yuzhang Shang, Zhen Dong, Emilio Ferrara

candidates.title: Embedding Models Measure in Peculiar Ways
candidates.description: Embedding spaces define notions of semantic similarity and distance. We study whether those embeddings reflect physical measurements of mass, distance, time and volume, which admit a unique, objective notion of semantic equivalence and distance. We find that physical measurement is only weakly modeled in the embedding space, and that instead quite peculiar measurement patterns can be observed. Further analysis indicates that embedding representations of physical measurements are strongly influenced by superficial string similarity, and recalibration of similarity does not substantially improve the alignment.
candidates.author: Juri Opitz, Andrianos Michail

candidates.title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision
candidates.description: Complex robotic manipulation tasks frequently require a long-term memory of past events and actions. As conditioning on full histories renders policies prone to spurious correlations and degrades performance, many approaches to policy memory involve compressing historical information through expensive VLM queries in-the-loop to process only task-salient information. In this paper, we propose an alternative approach in which computationally intensive VLM queries are made during train-time to learn a lightweight latent memory that can be efficiently queried at deployment time. Our representation, which we call the \textbf{workspace token}, is trained by (1) using a VLM to identify current and historical information necessary for completing a task, then (2) distilling these into the workspace token using a set-reconstruction decoder loss. In both simulation and hardware, we show that the workspace token can be used as a drop-in replacement for observations during deployment, enabling policies to solve memory-intensive tasks without the need for VLM reasoning in-the-loop. Interestingly, we found that workspace tokens are not only more lightweight but also lead to better policy performance.
candidates.author: Nitish Dashora, Douglas Chen, Idan Shenfeld, John Marangola, Pulkit Agrawal, Max Simchowitz

candidates.title: FAMOS: Feed-Forward 3D Articulation Modeling from Sparse Observations
candidates.description: Modeling articulated objects from sparse monocular views is challenging because each observation reveals only partial geometry and motion evidence. Most feed-forward methods infer articulation from a single observation and therefore rely heavily on learned category-level shape priors. We present FAMOS, a feed-forward model that predicts movable-part segmentation and joint parameters from a sparse, unordered set of partial point clouds. Our model jointly reasons over multiple observations and naturally supports a variable number of inputs, including a single view. To aggregate articulation cues across observations, we introduce a Multi-state Articulation Transformer with alternating state-wise and global attention. We further propose an observed articulation span objective that supervises the motion range each part exhibits across the input observations, encouraging the model to leverage the full observation set. To overcome the limited scale and diversity of existing datasets, we introduce a procedural data generator that synthesizes self-annotated assets during training. Experiments on PartNet-Mobility, ACD, and ArtiCraft-10K demonstrate consistent improvements over both feed-forward and optimization-based baselines. Project page: https://kevinqu7.github.io/famos
candidates.author: Kevin Qu, Tao Sun, Massimiliano Viola, Liyuan Zhu, Zhizhuo Zhou, Sayan Deb Sarkar, Konrad Schindler, Iro Armeni

candidates.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
candidates.description: Professional design requires any-color control: the ability to specify an object's target color with any 24-bit hex value for image generation and editing. Prior work has explored color generation, editing, and colorization, but often relies on dedicated color representations or specialized inference procedures. Advances in large language models offer a simpler starting point: even compact models can associate hex values with color semantics. We present Paint-Anything, which learns a shared hex-prompt interface for generation and editing through object-level color supervision. We develop a data pipeline that constructs Paint-500K from real images through object grounding, perceptual color labeling, and editing-pair synthesis. Since shadows make real-image labels only approximate colors, we complement this supervision with pure-color anchors whose pixels exactly match their paired hex values. These anchors are used only at high-noise timesteps, leaving low-noise training to natural images. We further introduce Any Color Benchmark (ACBench), comprising ACBench-T2I and ACBench-Edit, to measure object-level hex color fidelity across both tasks. On FLUX.2-4B, Paint-Anything improves ACBench-T2I and ACBench-Edit scores by 85.3% and 28.3%, respectively, relative to the base model, with ablations supporting the training recipe. It also achieves the highest average CompColor score among the compared methods.
candidates.author: Ji Xie, Dewei Zhou, Xinyu Huang, Zhennan Chen, Xun Wang

candidates.title: ERCPMP-Gx: Endoscopic Image and Video Dataset for Morphological, Histopathological, and Genomic Characterization of Colorectal Polyposis
candidates.description: Hereditary polyposis syndromes can be precursor lesions to colorectal cancer and are associated with a broad spectrum of extracolonic tumors. Early identification and accurate classification of these syndromes are essential for timely diagnosis, individualized patient management, and targeted surveillance strategies for affected families. However, public endoscopic datasets are largely organized around the individual sporadic polyp, and none links the polyposis phenotype to histopathology and germline findings at the patient level. Here, we present ERCPMP-Gx, an endoscopic, histopathological, and genomic dataset developed to support the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in the recognition, characterization, and classification of colorectal polyposis. Most procedures were performed using the Olympus EVIS X1 system with white-light endoscopy (WLE), narrow-band imaging (NBI), magnifying NBI (M-NBI), and NBI with near focus modes, yielding 160 images and accompanying video clips. Approximately eighty percent of cases represent clinically and/or genetically confirmed hereditary polyposis syndromes (PG), including familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS), juvenile polyposis syndrome (JPS), and ganglioneuroma syndrome (GNS), while the remaining twenty percent comprise non-hereditary polyps and polyp-mimicking lesions with overlapping morphological features (Non-PG), included to support differential classification. Each released record is linked, where available, to standardized endoscopic annotations, representative histopathology, and clinically reported germline findings, forming an AI-ready, patient-level annotation framework. The dataset is publicly accessible at Mendeley (https://doi.org/10.17632/nzyfc544bx.2). For the latest updates and further information, readers are referred to the DataBioX website: https://databiox.com.
candidates.author: Zahra Ghaffari, Massih Bahar, Mojgan Forootan, Ali Darvishi, Hamidreza Bolhasani

candidates.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
candidates.description: Frontier coding agents are increasingly trusted to work autonomously for long periods, yet an agent's final response is often the only account of that work a user sees. We quantify the propensity of frontier agents to \emph{overclaim} task completion, a misrepresentation that can mislead the user. An agent overclaims when its final response contradicts information in its context. This definition requires no inference about intent and is independent of task success. We introduce \emph{OverclaimBench}, an evaluation suite composed of five file-review scenarios, transcript-based coverage measurements, and registered planted defects. We evaluate eight proprietary frontier models in their own production command-line interfaces, and four open-weight models under a single fixed harness on OverclaimBench and find that 1) agents do not read all the files they were asked to review in 67.9\% of runs; 2) among runs where not all files are read, agents are \emph{misleading} 80.4\% of the time (59--96\% per model), either falsely claiming to have read all files or omitting that coverage is incomplete; 3) requiring delegation to subagents increased reading coverage, but among reviews that remained incomplete, a large majority were still misleading; and 4) agents that falsely claimed a complete review missed planted defects at about 1.8 times the rate of agents that read every file, showing that claims of completion can conceal substantive failures. Together, these results show that agents' final responses are not reliable accounts of their actions.
candidates.author: Nolan Smyth, Yorguin-Jose Mantilla-Ramos, Pascal Jr Tikeng Notsawo, Saskia Helbling, Alberto Tosato, Mohamed Amine Merzouk, Nouha Dziri, Gauthier Gidel, Tommaso Tosato

candidates.title: Unifying Models of Intergroup Hostility in Online Discourse
candidates.description: Hostile rhetoric toward social groups can normalize exclusion and justify mistreatment, as well as contribute to rising polarization and political violence. Efforts to moderate hostile rhetoric in online speech draw on foundational theories in social and moral psychology, and political science. However, these theories were developed largely in parallel, often propose different and sometimes conflicting accounts of how hostility develops, and have rarely been tested against each other in real discourse. The result is a fragmented understanding of the rhetorical mechanisms of hostility, without a clear sense of how they appear, and relate to each other, in real-world discourse. Using 2.86 million posts from TikTok, Truth Social, and Twitter/X during the 2024 U.S. presidential election, we model the mechanisms of six foundational theories of intergroup hostility -- boundary construction, threat construction, scapegoating, negative evaluation, dehumanization, and action orientation -- within a common empirical framework to recover the broader organization of intergroup hostility rhetoric. Structurally, we find that boundary construction and threat construction anchor the system; temporally, we find that these mechanisms tend to follow a regular ordering: boundary construction, derogation, and action orientation tend to appear early; dehumanization and threat construction later; scapegoating latest. Mapping how these theoretical frameworks actually manifest in discourse bridges longstanding divisions across social science traditions and presents computational social science with a clearer empirical foundation for modeling intergroup hostility rhetoric beyond single-label detection.
candidates.author: Patrick Gerard, Julia Mendelsohn, Kristina Lerman

candidates.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
candidates.description: Coding harnesses shape how autonomous coding agents translate model capabilities into long-horizon software-engineering performance, yet existing work typically evaluates harnesses as monolithic systems, leaving the effectiveness of individual components unclear. To enable component-level comparisons, we study this question with a lightweight coding harness whose execution loop is fixed while three components are varied: planning, action space, and context management. Across four models evaluated on SWE-Bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.1, we evaluate 176 matched settings spanning five context-management strategies, four context-window budgets, and targeted ablations of planning and action space. We find that: (1) Context management becomes increasingly valuable as the context-window budget tightens, with most of its benefit coming from preventing context-overflow failures. (2) Staging rule-based elision before LLM-based summarization provides the strongest overall efficiency among the context-management strategies, whereas making elided content recoverable adds machinery that models rarely use and yields no accuracy gain. (3) Planning shifts from an accuracy scaffold for weaker models to a cost saver for stronger models, with little change in accuracy. (4) Predefined tools improve performance for models with weaker bash proficiency, whereas bash-capable models can operate effectively with a bash-only interface and achieve substantially lower cost, especially on command-line-centric tasks. Trajectory-level analysis explains these effects: context management extends execution trajectories without substantially altering agent behavior, planning changes where trajectories stop, and the action space changes the granularity at which code is written. These findings inform model- and budget-aware harness design and provide a modular framework for evaluating future harness components.
candidates.author: Run-Ze Fan, Zihao Zhang, Simin Ma, Yebowen Hu, Shouju Wang, Kaiqiang Song, Fei Liu, Hamed Zamani, Xiaoyang Wang

candidates.title: JEPA-Anything: Learning Predictive Models across Different Worlds
candidates.description: World modeling enables intelligence to anticipate consequences, guide interventions, and learn from interaction. Yet predictive models remain domain-specific: can a common learning principle support world modeling across radically different systems? We introduce JEPA-Anything, a domain-agnostic framework based on orthogonal predictive factorization (OPF). Extending joint-embedding predictive architectures, OPF decomposes latent targets into complementary factors, learns them through dedicated pathways, and recombines them within a shared predictive design. We evaluate JEPA-Anything across seven domains: vision, biology, clinical trajectories, control, molecular dynamics, physical fields, and weather. Experiments span representation learning, intervention prediction, out-of-distribution generalization, and long-horizon dynamics, including 10 matched dynamics tasks, forecasting of over 1,000 clinical events, and 100-step molecular rollouts across four systems. Against matched JEPA baselines, JEPA-Anything improves reported metrics on all 10 dynamics tasks and reduces single-intervention prediction error on Interventional Pong by 34.8%. It achieves the lowest one-step and 100-step molecular errors among compared methods in all four systems. Beyond prediction, a factor-nominated biological intervention receives experimental support in cell co-cultures, patient-derived organoids, tumor fragments, and mice; latent orbital modes recover the Keplerian scaling exponent with a fitted slope of -1.4991. These results support a common factorized predictive principle across heterogeneous worlds, connecting world modeling with intervention and experimentally grounded scientific discovery. Code: https://github.com/Gen-Verse/JEPA-Anything
candidates.author: Taoyong Cui, Zhongyao Wang, Xinyue Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhaochen Yu, Yuying Zhang, Qiang Gao, Mengyue Yang, Wanli Ouyang, Pheng Ann Heng, Yingcheng Wu, Zhenfei Yin, Ling Yang

candidates.title: StageGuard: Learning Stage Transitions for Long-Horizon Robot Tasks via Agentic Distillation
candidates.description: Hierarchical planning frameworks combine skills from multiple robot control policies for long-horizon task execution, where determining when to terminate the current skill and advance to the next subtask is essential. Existing approaches often rely on pre-designed completion signal checkers that are hard to obtain in real-world execution. Large-scale vision-language models (VLMs) offer strong reasoning capabilities, but their decision boundaries are not inherently aligned with task completion criteria, while cloud deployment and lengthy reasoning introduce substantial latency, limiting real-time monitoring. We propose StageGuard, an agentic distillation framework for accurate and efficient stage-transition decisions. StageGuard combines teacher-model reasoning with demonstration trajectories to generate structured explanations of subtask completion and policy switching. A lightweight student VLM uses these explanations to generate compact self-explanations, which are used for supervised fine-tuning. We evaluate stage-transition prediction on trajectories from two benchmarks and assess closed-loop task success through integration into hierarchical robot control on BEHAVIOR-1K, with further validation on real robots. Results show substantial improvements in stage-transition prediction while supporting efficient online monitoring.
candidates.author: Jinbang Huang, Yuanzhao Hu, Zhiyuan Li, Ran Qi, Yixin Xiao, Yangzheng Wu, Tengyue Ba, Zhanguang Zhang, Yingxue Zhang

candidates.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
candidates.description: Multi-turn agents trained with reinforcement learning (RL) receive a single scalar reward per trajectory, which motivates self on-policy distillation (OPD) to supply dense token-level supervision from a self-teacher with privileged task skills, letting a skill-free student internalize them. This recipe, however, is undermined by two findings in agentic tasks: privileged information alone does not always make a teacher reliable, and the benefit of teacher supervision is stage-dependent. We therefore propose RetireOPD (Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation), which first optimizes a decoupled, skill-conditioned teacher with environment rewards and then trains a skill-free student jointly with RL and OPD. Rather than following a predefined distillation schedule, RetireOPD adopts Adaptive Retirement: the student drops the teacher on its own once their discrepancy stops shrinking and it reaches a target fraction of the teacher's success rate, after which training proceeds with RL alone. Across Qwen2.5 models from 1.5B to 7B, RetireOPD improves ALFWorld success rate over RL baseline by 14.1% to 18.8% and WebShop accuracy by 11.8% to 19.0%, and surpasses its own skill-conditioned teacher in every setting.
candidates.author: Yan Yu, Zhengxi Lu, Yizhou Liu, Yichen Pan, Aozhe Wang, Qipeng Chen, Hua Yang, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Qianglong Chen, Yongliang Shen
